خُلَّيْطَى : see خِلْطٌ. ―
-b2- وَقَعُوا فِى خُلَّيْطَى, (S, K,) and ↓ خُلَيْطَى , (K,) (assumed tropical:) They fell into a state of confusion: (K:) their affair, or case, became confused, or perplexed, (اِخْتَلَطَ,) to them. (S.) And ↓ كُنَّا خُلَيْطَى (assumed tropical:) [We were in a state of confusion]: cited by Az, from an Arab of the desert. (TA.) [↓ خُلَّيْطَآءُ , which probably signifies the same, is mentioned in the TA, voce لُغَزٌ, on the authority of Sb.]
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
